solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fed tripe, I could become terror-stricken

indicators.note: the clue words may turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone served tripe is horrified at the plate in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' signals rearranging FED, TRIPE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone petrified is frozen with fear, exactly what terror-stricken describes.

clue.text: Place needing a boost (not showing any passion)

parts.note: PL is a standard abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
a tonic is something that gives a boost or pick-me-up

explanation.surface: A dull spot that needs perking up, with no excitement at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A platonic relationship is affectionate but free of romantic or sexual passion.

clue.text: Dessert soaked in alcohol — is it a rum possibly?

indicators.note: the letters could possibly form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the boozy pudding they are eating is laced with rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals rearranging IS IT A RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of sponge fingers soaked in coffee and liqueur.

clue.text: At home, woman needs to match a colour

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
to go with something is to match it, so go can mean match

explanation.surface: A woman at home wants a paint shade to match her decor.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet shade, one of the seven rainbow colours.

clue.text: One mouse finally put in enclosure when it gets very cold

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: put in means that letter goes inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word mouse

explanation.surface: A pet mouse is moved into its cage when winter turns bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places E, the last letter of mouse (from 'finally'), inside CAGE, after I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice age is a long period of glaciation when the earth becomes very cold.

clue.text: Opinionated scoundrel has mum twitching

parts.note: a dog is an old word for a worthless scoundrel
ma is an informal word for mother or mum
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A bossy rogue makes his mother nervous enough to twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatic means asserting opinions as if they were unquestionable, so opinionated is a close synonym.

clue.text: Evident in room — Phyllis's sex-appeal

indicators.note: the answer can be seen within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Phyllis's allure is obvious to everyone in the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evident in' signals the answer sitting inside rOOM PHyllis's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for energy and attractiveness, often sexual allure.

clue.text: What's troubled lad so? Weird heritage site

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or weird

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is upsetting a young man at a strange old ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges LAD SO into OLDSA. OLD SARUM is an abandoned hill-fort and early city site near Salisbury in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Sarum is a historic ruined settlement in Wiltshire cared for as a heritage attraction.

clue.text: Large expanse of water in a holy city

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea, a large body of water

explanation.surface: A sacred city is said to stand in a vast sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Medina in Saudi Arabia is the second holiest city in Islam.

clue.text: Where synod squashes unorthodox belief

indicators.note: the two words squash the answer between them, so it lies within their letters

explanation.surface: A church council clamps down on a heretical doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside wHERE SYnod.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief contrary to accepted religious doctrine.

clue.text: Contract made in a card game

parts.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A deal agreed over a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is a verb here, not the bridge term it pretends to be.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or contract it.

clue.text: Armies start to chat, it being arranged?

definitions.text: Armies start to chat, it being arranged?

indicators.note: being arranged means the letters are put into a new order
the start of the word chat is its first letter

explanation.surface: Opposing armies begin talking, with a deal being set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being arranged' rearranges ARMIES, C (from 'start to chat') and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce agreed between warring sides, which is what armies talking would arrange.

clue.text: The most important person not everyone found to be unpleasant

parts.note: number one, written NO 1, is the most important person
some means not all, so not everyone

explanation.surface: The top dog is found disagreeable by a fair number of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of NO 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disagreeable, especially of smells.

clue.text: Two sailors having year in historical region long ago

parts.note: tar is a slang word for a sailor
the second tar, another sailor

explanation.surface: A pair of seamen spend a year in an old distant land.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartary was the old European name for the vast region of Central Asia ruled by Tartars.

clue.text: More than 'no bread', but much less than 'half a loaf'?

definitions.text: More than 'no bread', but much less than 'half a loaf'?

parts.words: More than 'no bread', but much less than 'half a loaf'?
parts.note: plays on the proverb that half a loaf is better than no bread: a tiny scrap of reassurance is more than nothing but far short of half

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'half a loaf is better than no bread' means something is better than nothing; the answer is read literally as bread fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Small consolations in a bad situation, literally little pieces of bread lying between nothing and half a loaf.

clue.text: Cork has a humble dwelling

parts.note: a bung is a stopper, like a cork
low can mean humble in rank or status

explanation.surface: Someone from Cork lives in a modest house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cork' looks like the Irish city but is a stopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey house, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Escort who could make tour dire

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guide whose presence would ruin a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges TOUR DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrider is a mounted or motorcycle escort riding beside a vehicle.

clue.text: Musical state

definitions.meaning: a Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of 1943
a US state in the south-central plains

explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is both a famous stage musical and the US state it is named after.

clue.text: Brawny group not very bright up top

indicators.note: in a down clue, up top places this piece above the other one

parts.note: thick is informal for stupid, not very bright
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A muscular gang lacking intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very bright up top' reads as one phrase about a dim head, but 'up top' is a placing signal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset means heavily and solidly built, close to brawny.

clue.text: Pet going round English writer knocked over item of furniture

indicators.note: going round means the pet word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet

indicators.note: in an across clue, knocked over means the word for writer is turned backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A pet wandering round knocks over an English author and a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a verb of affection, but it is the animal; 'knocked over' means turned backwards in this across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Copper places an embargo on islanders

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
bans means forbids, which is what an embargo does

explanation.surface: A policeman forbids trade with island people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubans live on Cuba, a Caribbean island, so they are islanders.

clue.text: Cake time at school unending for him!

definitions.text: Cake time at school unending for him!

parts.note: a bun is a small sweet cake

indicators.note: unending means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a term is a period of time at school

explanation.surface: Endless cake through the school term would delight him.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a greedy fat schoolboy in British comic stories by Frank Richards, forever after cake. 'unending' cuts the M from TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue as a whole describes the cake-obsessed schoolboy of British fiction.

clue.text: B-Bill having ailment, one on account of these?

definitions.text: B-Bill having ailment, one on account of these?

parts.note: a stammered B plus AC, short for account, which is a bill
ill is an ailment or illness
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stammering Bill falls sick, and these germs are to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter gives a lone B; 'Bill' is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, some of which cause disease, so illness can be on account of them.

clue.text: Work under small section to secure good tent

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the work piece below the rest
to secure means to hold the good letter tightly inside

parts.note: a bit is a small piece or section
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Labouring beneath a small piece of fabric to fasten a decent shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work under' reads like a job description; 'under' is a placing signal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A big top is the large tent of a circus.

clue.text: Firm operating, having circumvented road barrier

indicators.note: having circumvented means the outer letters go round the road letters

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A working company gets round a roadblock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm operating' reads as a business at work, but splits into two short abbreviations that go round the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon is a line of police or guards forming a barrier.

clue.text: Headline about old rockers holding together

parts.note: a rock band is a group of rockers
aging means growing old

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about veteran rock musicians still sticking together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headline about old rockers' is how BAND AGING would read as a news headline: noun first, then the verb for getting old.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandaging is binding a wound with strips of cloth, holding it together.

clue.text: Dull outside must be transformed

indicators.note: the word must be transformed into another, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The outdoors is boring and needs a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be transformed' rearranges OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious means boring or dull.

clue.text: One of the good guys, Green politician

parts.note: St is short for saint, a very good person
raw can mean green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A good guy who is a Green Party politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw is a former British Labour cabinet minister; 'Green' looks like the party but means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Straw was a long-serving British politician, Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary.

clue.text: Sorry writer volunteers to appear in break

indicators.note: to appear in means these letters are placed inside the break word

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break
a pen is a writing instrument
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: An apologetic author has volunteers turn up during a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' reads as a pause in work, but here means a tear in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Repentant means regretful for wrongdoing, which is what sorry means.
